about: Everyone on the team that runs Web Summit 2026, human and agent, and who works with whom. Seven people are going to Lisbon (Dinis Cruz, Silvio Switha, Nimay Parekh, Vicky, Jose Bota, Angelo and Indi Gupte), working with a designer (Sarah) and a first friendly (Daniela), each with their own agent; the team's agents work for them on a schedule. The roles come from [the team brief](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/web-summit-team-brief.html) and the people from [part two](https://newsroom.sgit.ai/articles/web-summit-humans-and-their-agents.html). From 2 November 2026, at the operator's word, the team's members are named here (only the team uses this site, and speed matters); still no contact details, ever. Each person's brief, and the issues they can pick up: [the briefs](../briefs/index.html). Kept by the conductor.

members.reviewed_by: to decide: one of the seven reviews its output daily
members.summary: Opens and closes every wake, chooses which roles run in it, routes requests, keeps the schedule, the keys, the build, the gate and the site true, and writes the daily debrief. Held by conductor.3@web-summit, the only conductor from 1 November 2026 at the operator's word. Before it, conductor.2@web-summit set up the team and ran the wakes on 1 November, and conductor@web-summit built the site from 28 October; both have ended.
owns: the wake: the opening plan, the sub-agents it runs, the closing check
the release: version.txt, versions.json, the pipeline

REALITY.md and the session log
rules: Write only the paths in policy.json.
Public material only; every fact with its source and the date read.
Nothing private about a person: no contact detail, ever.
Push to dev only; main is the operator's call.
Fetch dev before every release, so two sessions never race a version number.
A red validate is no release; never disable a check to get green.

members.name: The inbox agent
members.summary: Manages the operator's inbox and drafts the replies the operator sends. Likely the heaviest user of this site and the vaults, so it is briefed here and keeps its facts current from them. Its public key will be published by the operator. Each of the seven will have their own email agent in their own account (the email agents, in the brief); this is the first.
owns: the drafts in the operator's drafts folder
the note that goes with each draft: what it used, what it could not confirm
its own outbox in the mail vault
rules: No agent sends email: it drafts, a person sends.
It states only facts the site or a vault supports, and says what is to be confirmed.
Consent and contact details: nothing about a person goes public without their yes.
